tools.name: search
tools.description: Full-text search across every post and blog in the directory. Returns matching blogs and matching individual posts, each with the identifiers read_post needs. tools.name: list_feeds
tools.description: Page through the whole directory, newest first. Narrow to one category with kind: blog, news, podcast, music, video, comic, live or reel. The category is decided from the feed document on every crawl, never from what the submitter claimed.

tools.name: get_feed
tools.description: One blog or podcast: its metadata, who writes it, where it can be found elsewhere, the topics it is filed under — including the ones no other feed shares — and its recent posts. `authors` is people; `links` is the blog's own accounts, which is what an unsigned blog has instead. tools.name: list_topics
tools.description: What the directory covers, by how many feeds cover it. Pass query to search the index instead of paging it. Only subjects at least two feeds share are indexed — a topic one blog uses is that blog's own vocabulary, and lives on its page instead. Raise min to find the well-covered subjects.

tools.name: get_topic
tools.description: Every feed filed under one topic. The keyword is normalised, so "Home Lab", "home lab" and "home-lab" all reach the same topic and you can pass a phrase you read anywhere. Each feed says whether it landed here from the publisher's own tag or from a phrase counted across its writing. A comma-separate

tools.name: topic_posts
tools.description: What the feeds covering a topic have actually published lately, newest first — the river rather than the roster. Note the difference from get_topic, which lists who covers the subject; this lists what they wrote. Drawn from the feeds most strongly filed under the topic, so a very broad keyword is a

tools.name: read_post
tools.description: The full text of one post, extracted from the publisher's own page and returned as prose. Takes the feed slug and post guid that search, get_feed and topic_posts return. tools.name: random_feed
tools.description: One feed from the directory, chosen at random, with its recent posts. The web without a ranking function: what is here rather than what is popular.

tools.name: list_authors
tools.description: The directory's authors and where else they publish — their own sites, Mastodon and Bluesky accounts, GitHub, links pages. Every link was published by the author on their own site as a rel="me" claim, an h-card or JSON-LD; nothing is scraped from a platform or bought. Filter with network to find onl

tools.name: get_author
tools.description: One person: where to find them, and everything in the directory they publish. The feed list is what settles whether two people with the same name are the same person.

tools.name: get_openprofile
tools.description: The person as a portable profile file (logicsrc.com/openprofile): identity block, Accounts, Topics, a Broadcast section (logicsrc.com/openbroadcast) for every show they publish, corrected by the person once they have claimed it. Returns the Markdown and the parsed sections. Pass either the author's

tools.name: update_openprofile
tools.description: Edit a profile you have claimed. Send the whole file as `markdown` (everything in it becomes your word; a section you leave out is dropped) or a patch: `headline`, `identity` {Key: value, or null to remove}, `sections` {name: Markdown body, or null to drop}, `public`. tools.name: claim_openprofile
tools.description: Say that an author in this directory is you, so you can correct the profile. Verified on the spot, no reviewer: the email behind your credential matches the address the author published about themselves, or the author's own site links back at the profile with rel="openprofile" or rel="me". Needs a c

tools.name: directory_stats
tools.description: How big the directory is, what it is made of, and whether the crawler is keeping up. `stale` is active feeds not read successfully in a day; `due` is a backlog that should drain within a tick or two. Answer this before concluding a feed is missing — it may simply not have been crawled yet.

tools.name: trending_topics
tools.description: Subjects English blogs and news sites used in headlines more than the week before, ranked. `count` is feeds, not posts, in a one in four sample, so it measures movement rather than coverage, and `prior_count` is the same figure for the week before. Updated daily. An empty list means the rollup has n

tools.name: list_rings
tools.description: The OpenWebring rings hosted here (logicsrc.com/openwebring): one per well-covered topic, each an ordered circular list of member sites with next, previous and random hops. Every entry carries the ring page, the ring file, an OPML of the members' feeds, and how many members are listed and active. A

tools.name: get_ring
tools.description: A ring's members in ring order, each with its site, feed, status (active, pending or inactive) and, where the site declared them, made_by and disclosure. The same document as /ring/<slug>/openwebring.json. Use ring_next to follow a hop rather than computing one from this list.

tools.name: ring_next
tools.description: Which member a hop lands on, without following a redirect: the site after or before `from` in ring order, or a random one. `from` is a member site URL or its slug; omit it for a random active member. Pending and inactive members are listed by get_ring but skipped here, and the ring wraps around. Not

tools.name: ring_embed
tools.description: The copy-paste HTML a site puts in its footer to show it belongs to one or more webrings here: `<< Ring >>` per ring, previous / ring page / next, each hop measured from the member site given as `site` (its homepage). Returns a plain variant (bare links, the page styles them) and a styled one (inlin

tools.name: get_newsletter
tools.description: RSSAmp's weekly email: when it goes (day and hour, UTC), the next send, how many accounts are on it, and the latest issue as sent (subject and text). Every account is on it unless it opted out.

tools.name: newsletter_preview
tools.description: This week's digest as it would be built right now from the directory: new feeds, posts from the most-followed blogs, liked posts, webring activity. Read-only: nothing is stored or sent. `issue` is null when there is nothing to say yet.

tools.name: submit_feed
tools.description: Submit one URL or a list of them to RSSAmp. A site URL works as well as a feed URL: the feed is discovered from the page. Anyone may submit; there is no account and no review queue. One URL resolves in the call and the answer carries its page; a list may be queued, and the answer says which. Rate li

tools.name: list_webhooks
tools.description: Your webhook endpoints (url, event filters, on/off, failures) and the event types this site emits. Needs one of your rssamplifier API keys in the Authorization header (Bearer rsa_..., from /account).

tools.name: create_webhook
tools.description: Register an https URL to receive your alerts as signed POSTs (CloudEvents body, Standard Webhooks signature headers, plus x-rssamplifier-signature: sha256=<hex HMAC of the body>). Returns the endpoint and its signing secret (whsec_...), shown here once. Needs one of your rssamplifier API keys in the

tools.name: update_webhook
tools.description: Change an endpoint's url, events, description, or switch it on/off (turning it back on clears its failure count). Needs one of your rssamplifier API keys in the Authorization header (Bearer rsa_..., from /account).

tools.name: delete_webhook
tools.description: Delete an endpoint and its delivery log. Needs one of your rssamplifier API keys in the Authorization header (Bearer rsa_..., from /account).

tools.name: test_webhook
tools.description: Send a signed webhook.test event to the endpoint now and report the HTTP status. Needs one of your rssamplifier API keys in the Authorization header (Bearer rsa_..., from /account).

tools.name: rotate_webhook_secret
tools.description: Mint a new signing secret for the endpoint and return it; the old one stops working at once. Needs one of your rssamplifier API keys in the Authorization header (Bearer rsa_..., from /account).

tools.name: webhook_deliveries
tools.description: Recent deliveries (status, attempts, last HTTP status or error, payload), for one endpoint or all of yours. Needs one of your rssamplifier API keys in the Authorization header (Bearer rsa_..., from /account).

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "search" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "update_openprofile" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: search, list_feeds, get_feed, list_topics, get_topic, topic_posts, read_post, list_authors, get_author, get_openprofile, directory_stats, trending_topics, list_rings, get_ring, get_newsletter, newsletter_preview, submit_feed, list_webhooks, create_webhook · Private data: list_feeds, read_post, get_openprofile, update_openprofile, claim_openprofile, list_rings, get_ring, list_webhooks, create_webhook, update_webhook, delete_webhook, test_webhook, rotate_webhook_secret, webhook_deliveries · Public sink: search, get_feed, list_topics, read_post, list_authors, get_author, get_openprofile, update_openprofile, claim_openprofile, get_newsletter, submit_feed, list_webhooks, create_webhook, update_webhook, delete_webhook, test_webhook, rotate_webhook_secret, webhook_deliveries · Destructive: update_openprofile, delete_webhook.

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
